subject: Per-token phasing & monthly commit schedule for Launchly - negotiation
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@launchly.com>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Launch plan — expected token ramp + pricing ask

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed by the latency profiles and the batching options. We're working on the internal launch plan for Q3 and wanted to get a clearer picture of how Redwood's per-token discounts can align with our seasonal ramp. Two quick asks: 

- Can you share a sample monthly phasing schedule (step-up commits) that would allow us to start conservative in month 1 and double usage month-over-month through month 4?
- What is the discount cadence for per-token pricing at those steps (e.g., 0-1B, 1-3B, 3-8B tokens)? We have a high-read/write ratio and want to make sure the math works for our pricing model.

I've attached a preliminary forecast (Launchly_usage_forecast_q3-q4.xlsx) that shows expected spikes around product launch. Procurement is CC'd so they can start a checklist if the economics look right.

Thanks — can we sync next week for 30 minutes?

Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Platform Partnerships, Launchly

From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@launchly.com>
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, procurement@launchly.com
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Launch plan — expected token ramp + pricing ask

Samir — thanks for the forecast and for looping procurement in. I dropped a quick sketch below of a phasing option that has worked well for similar launches; happy to walk through the numbers on a call.

Quick sketch (monthly commit / per-token discount):
- Month 1: 0.5B tokens committed — baseline price (no discount)
- Month 2: 1.25B tokens committed — 8% per-token discount on incremental tokens
- Month 3: 2.5B tokens committed — 12% discount on incremental tokens
- Month 4+: 5B committed (steady state) — 18% discount on incremental tokens and a surge buffer policy for 20% above commit at a blended surcharge of 25% of list

Notes:
- We can structure as a monthly commit with step-up windows (you lock each next month by day 20 of the current month).
- True-ups are monthly; we offer a 30% credit pool for launch-related overages in month 1 if you commit to a 6-month ramp schedule.

Attachments I'm about to share: our internal "Redwood_Commit_Tiers_v3.xlsx" with the exact per-token breakpoints. Propose Tuesday 7/6 at 10am PT for a 30-min call — does that work?

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference

From: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 08:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Launch plan — expected token ramp + pricing ask

Vanessa — forwarding Samir's forecast. A couple internal things to confirm before the call: 

1) Margin floor on the four-tier phasing above — Rishi, can we guarantee the 18% peak discount if the customer signs a 6-month commit with the step-up guardrails?
2) Surge protection wording — legal typically prefers a hard cap on surge buffer (e.g., 15% above commit) vs blended surcharge. If we offer 20% buffer for launch month, legal will want to see the MSA redlines.

I'll join the call as well.

— Neha
Head of Dedicated Sales Operations

From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
To: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 09:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Launch plan — expected token ramp + pricing ask

Neha / Vanessa — confirmed: we can commit to the 18% discount tier but only under the following constraints:

- 6-month minimum commitment window (monthly step-ups acceptable)
- Monthly true-up with invoice reconciliation; unpaid overages carry standard net-30 terms
- Launch surge buffer: 15% free buffer for the first launch month (no surcharge), additional surge up to 35% is allowed but billed at +30% of list per-token for the incremental amount above the 15% buffer.

I'll prepare a clean pricing appendix and push an MSA redline for legal to review. We should avoid offering a 30% blended surcharge as a blanket — pricing clarity is important for procurement.

Rishi
Head of Revenue Operations

From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@launchly.com>, procurement@launchly.com
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 06 Jul 2027 10:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Launch plan — expected token ramp + pricing ask

Samir — thanks for your time today. Per our call, summary of what Redwood can offer for Launchly's Q3 launch: 

- Commitment structure: 6-month agreement with monthly step-up windows (you confirm next month's commit by the 20th).
- Month-by-month example (from the forecast you shared): M1 0.5B; M2 1.25B; M3 2.5B; M4 5B.
- Discounts: incremental discounts applied by bracket; peak confirmed at 18% for >=3B bracket when under a 6-month commitment.
- Surge policy: 15% complimentary buffer for first launch month. Additional surge up to +35% allowed but billed at list * 1.30 for incremental tokens (above the 15% buffer).
- Onboarding credit: one-time $10k credit applied to month 1 invoice if you sign by July 20.
- Attachments: 
  - Redwood_Commit_Tiers_v3.xlsx (pricing matrix)
  - Proposed MSA redline (MSA_redline_v2.pdf) — legal to review
  - Your forecast (Launchly_usage_forecast_q3-q4.xlsx) confirmed received

Next steps: please confirm the example monthly commits and whether procurement wants the redlines incorporated into their SOW/PO flow. We'll issue a DocuSign link for the MSA + pricing appendix once you confirm.

Cheers,
Vanessa

From: procurement@launchly.com
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@launchly.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Launch plan — expected token ramp + pricing ask

Vanessa — procurement here. Reviewed internally with finance and legal. A couple clarifying asks before we sign: 

1) Can the complimentary buffer be extended to two months at 10% each instead of a single 15% month? That helps smooth the billing impact across both spike and pre-launch testing.
2) For the step-up confirmation window, can we move the deadline to the 25th rather than the 20th? Our internal procurement approval cycle needs a little more lead time.

If you can accept those two small changes, we are good to proceed and will complete signatures this week. We've attached our PO template in the HubSpot deal and will expect the DocuSign once the MSA redlines incorporate the buffer change.

Thanks — procurement@launchly.com
